name: Henderson Guitar Shop
cost: Free to visit, guitars by waitlist
unique: The workshop of a luthier who has built guitars for Eric Clapton and Doc Watson out of a shed in a Grayson County hollow, where he will show you the spruce tops he taps for tone and the neck blanks drying above the stove.
buzz: Visitors describe being handed a guitar to play and staying two hours. He is a legendary picker as well as a builder, and the wait for one of his instruments is measured in years.

name: Wayne C. Henderson Music Festival and Guitar Competition
customer: Bluegrass and old time fans, pickers, families
unique: A one day festival in the picnic area at Grayson Highlands where the guitar competition is the main event, with contestants playing for a hand built Henderson guitar and a lineup of Appalachian musicians who come because they know him.
buzz: The competition draws serious pickers and the crowd sits on the grass in the shade. People call it the friendliest festival in the state and the raffle guitar is the reason many buy tickets.

name: Comers Rock Overlook
dates: Year round, forest road may be rough
company: George Washington and Jefferson National Forests
unique: A stone fire tower on a 4,102 foot knob at the edge of the Mount Rogers high country, with a catwalk view over the New River valley and ridges stacked to the horizon, reached by a short walk from a forest road.
buzz: Locals send visitors here instead of the crowded park overlooks. The tower steps are steep and the road up is gravel, which keeps the crowd down.

name: Virginia Creeper Trail
company: Town of Damascus and the U.S. Forest Service
unique: A rail trail on the old Abingdon branch line, mostly downhill, crossing thirty trestles and running along Whitetop Laurel Creek through a gorge, with shuttle outfits in Damascus hauling riders and bikes to the top.
buzz: The sixteen mile Abingdon to Damascus stretch is open and the seventeen mile Damascus to Whitetop section is closed for Hurricane Helene repairs until April 2027. Rentals and shuttles are running for the open section.

name: Damascus Trail Days
customer: Thru hikers, section hikers, gear nerds
unique: The largest Appalachian Trail festival in the country, held in a town the trail runs straight through, with a hiker parade, gear vendors, free food lines and thousands of thru hikers walking in from the woods.
buzz: Hikers plan their whole year around it and locals open their yards. The parade of hikers through town is the photograph, and the gear repairs are free.

name: William King Museum of Art
customer: Art people, regional history fans, families
unique: A free museum in a former school building with galleries of Appalachian decorative arts and regional painting, a studio wing for classes, and a permanent collection that treats southwest Virginia furniture and pottery as fine art.
buzz: Free admission and a serious craft collection. Visitors are surprised by the quality and by how much of it is local, and the gift shop is where people buy regional pottery.

name: Virginia Highlands Festival
cost: Free to browse, some events ticketed
dates: Late July into early August, about ten days
unique: Ten days of juried craft shows, antiques, author talks, music and theatre across Abingdon, running since 1949 and using the whole town, including the Barter Theatre and the historic district, as its venue.
buzz: The antiques and craft market is the draw and people come back every year for specific dealers. Locals complain about parking and go anyway.

name: Hungry Mother State Park
dates: Year round, beach Memorial Day–Labor Day
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
unique: One of the six original Virginia state parks, built by the CCC around a mountain lake with a sand beach, a restaurant on the water, cabins and trails that climb to a rock overlook of the whole valley.
buzz: The lake beach and the restaurant are why families return, and the cabin reservations open a year out and go fast. The name comes from a legend about a woman and her child that the park does not oversell.

name: Lincoln Theatre
dates: Year round, season plus film nights
customer: Music fans, film people, families at holiday shows
unique: A 1929 movie palace with a restored neon marquee and Spanish colonial interior on Marion's main street, reopened as a performing arts center that books bluegrass, country and touring acts and still runs films.
buzz: The restoration and the acoustics get the praise, and the Crooked Road music shows are the local favorites. The marquee is the photograph of downtown.

name: Museum of the Middle Appalachians
unique: A museum built around the salt marsh and fossil beds at Saltville, where mammoth and mastodon bones and a 14,000 year old human footprint have come out of the same ground that later fed a Confederate salt works and a chemical plant.
buzz: The Ice Age fossils and the salt industry story in one small building is the appeal, and volunteers will explain the excavation history. It is a five dollar hour that surprises people.

name: Big Walker Lookout
unique: A hundred foot steel observation tower on the crest of Big Walker Mountain, built by a local family in the 1940s and still run by them, with a country store below selling candy, crafts and sandwiches and a view over five states on a clear day.
buzz: The tower sways a little and the stairs are open, which is either the appeal or the problem. The store's country ham biscuits and the birding from the deck are the recurring reviews.

name: Jackson Ferry Shot Tower
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
unique: A seventy five foot stone tower built in 1807 to drop molten lead through a sieve into water, making round shot for the frontier, standing on a cliff above the New River with the original shaft still inside.
buzz: The process is the interesting part and the setting on the river bluff is better than the tower itself. A short stop that photographers stretch out.

name: New River Trail State Park
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
unique: Fifty seven miles of crushed gravel on an abandoned railroad grade along the New River, one of the oldest rivers in North America, with tunnels, trestles, a shot tower and river access points spread across four counties.
buzz: Riders do the whole length in a day and families do the Galax end. The surface is smooth enough for hybrids and the tunnels are cool in summer.

name: Wolf Creek Indian Village and Museum
unique: A reconstruction of a Monacan village on the footprint of an excavated 16th century settlement, with palisade, longhouses, gardens and fire pits, interpreted by staff who explain what the archaeology actually found before the village was rebuilt.
buzz: The village is small and the guides are what make it, connecting the layout to the dig records. School groups fill it on weekdays in spring.

name: Dismal Creek Wilderness
company: George Washington and Jefferson National Forests
unique: A roadless pocket of the Jefferson National Forest where Dismal Creek runs clear over sandstone, with the Appalachian Trail following it for miles, brook trout in the pools and a waterfall a short walk from a forest road.
buzz: Quiet even in summer, and the creek is the reason. Anglers keep it to themselves and hikers use it as a gentle AT section.

name: Hillsville Labor Day Flea Market and Gun Show
dates: Labor Day weekend, Friday–Monday, plus Memorial Day
company: Hillsville Volunteer Fire Department and VFW
unique: One of the largest flea markets on the east coast, spreading over the fairground and every side street in a town of 2,700, with guns, antiques, tools, produce, fried food and livestock, run by volunteer fire and VFW groups as a fundraiser.
buzz: People come from a dozen states with trailers. Dealers say the good tools go Friday morning, and locals warn about the traffic on Route 58.

name: Hillsville Courthouse and the 1911 Shootout
customer: Local history people, true crime readers
unique: The courthouse where five people were killed in 1911 when the Allen family opened fire during a land dispute trial, a shootout that produced one of the largest manhunts in Virginia history and a folk ballad still sung in the county.
buzz: Locals tell the story better than any sign, and the bullet damage and the jail are the details people ask about. The annual play about the shootout draws a crowd.

name: Old Fiddler's Convention
unique: The oldest and largest old time and bluegrass convention in the world, six days of competitions in forty categories at Felts Park, with hundreds of musicians jamming under tarps and campers in the field until three in the morning.
buzz: Musicians describe it as the center of the old time universe and non musicians are surprised they can walk in and listen to world class picking for the price of a day ticket. Camping fills a year ahead.

name: Rex Theater
unique: A 1940 movie house on Galax's main street with an art deco marquee, restored as a live music room that books bluegrass, country and gospel and hosts the Friday night bluegrass series that locals treat as a standing appointment.
buzz: The sound in a small old theater is the review, and tickets are cheap. It is the year round answer to the festival crowd.

name: Birthplace of Country Music Museum
unique: A Smithsonian affiliate museum built on the story of the 1927 Bristol Sessions, when a talent scout recorded Jimmie Rodgers and the Carter Family in a hat factory and made the records that became country music, with listening stations for every session track.
buzz: The listening booths and the radio station inside are the highlight, and the museum makes the case for Bristol over Nashville without sneering. Musicians leave with a list of records to find.

name: Bristol Sign on State Street
customer: Roadside collectors, photographers, everyone passing through
unique: The neon sign over State Street that reads Bristol, A Good Place to Live and straddles the state line, so you can stand with one foot in Virginia and one in Tennessee under a landmark that has been photographed since the 1910s.
buzz: It is a two minute stop that everyone photographs, and the state line painted down the middle of the street is the other half of the ritual. Downtown has been rebuilt around it with breweries and shops.
